hypothesis: At model load, KleidiAI repacks every Q8_0 weight (requantisation to per-row int8 plus kai_run_rhs_pack_nxk_qsi8cxp_qsi8cx_neon) one tensor at a time on the loading thread, while 5 of the function's 6 vCPUs sit idle (the download has already finished). Splitting each tensor's repack into 6 nr-aligned row blocks on 6 threads cuts cold model_load_mmap from about 8.4 s to about 3-4 s (the repack is about 6 s of it; the rest is serial), with bytewise-identical packed weights and therefore bit-identical answers. Restore and warm should not change: the SnapStart snapshot is taken after the load. Reported either way.

changed_variable.baseline: 1: upstream's serial loops (P1's libraries in base; the patched libraries with GGML_KLEIDIAI_REPACK_THREADS unset in off, whose serial loops are upstream's text)
changed_variable.experiment: par: GGML_KLEIDIAI_REPACK_THREADS=6 (the vCPU count at 10,240 MB). Same zip as off, same configuration, same weights object; the packing routine and the packed bytes are unchanged

reproduce: # arm64 Linux host with Docker; P1's build/ (baseline/build.sh at 70eab7b) holds the pinned llama.cpp checkout and GGUF
aws s3api get-object --bucket <p1-bucket> --key code/26eb2651e8915f8ad09eae899feff583a448de6b8d2bc4943bccabb66cae189b/function.zip p1.zip   # and manifest.json -> p1-manifest.json
CPUSET=<6 idle cpus> examples/lambda-kleidiai/e8/hash_check.sh <p1-build>/model/s2b-h512-Q8_0.gguf 3   # offline, fixed host, not Lambda
CPUSET=<6 idle cpus> examples/lambda-kleidiai/e8/probe_e8.sh <p1-build>/model/s2b-h512-Q8_0.gguf 2   # offline answers vs P1's reference
conclusion: IMPROVED, cold start only (status rule disclosed in e8.status_rule; the pre-registered rule gives inconclusive). Six repack threads cut cold model_load_mmap on CPU part 0xd40 from 8.42 s to 2.88 s, and the cold first request (Init + Duration) from 36.00 s to 30.60 s (delta -5.41 s, 95% CI [-5.52, -5.34], n [44, 40]). Same sign in every round on every CPU part: 0xd0c -14.40 s (n [3, 6]), 0xd4f -4.32 s (n [3, 4]); those two strata are small. The load-phase part of the hypothesis (8.4 s to 3-4 s) held, and the result is below its range. The cold first request falls only by that saving, because the 25 s S3 download still runs before the load. Restore and warm do not change: restore first request -0.018 s [-0.047, +0.014], warm -0.016 s [-0.073, +0.073] on 0xd40. Max Memory Used unchanged. Init Duration unchanged (+0.001 s), because the on-demand load runs in PR #77's background thread after Init. The SnapStart snapshot init also loads faster, so publish_version is shorter, but restores replay the snapshot either way. Correctness: 1,800/1,800 answers bit-identical to P1's reference; all 320 loaded tensors (187 KleidiAI-packed, 1.89 GB) hash-identical to P1's libraries at 1, 2, 3 and 6 threads, offline. With the switch unset, the patched libraries match P1's on every headline stratum with n >= 5 per arm. Cost $3.53 at list prices. Host: three CPU parts observed (0xd40, 0xd0c, 0xd4f), split above; no generation is inferred from them.

e8.pairs_method: B minus A, medians within each CPU part (cpuinfo, read in the function) both arms ran on; ci95 = bootstrap over environments (4,000 resamples, seed 8); cells = per (round, CPU part) medians. Rows without a CPU part are counted, never a stratum. effect = par - off (the one variable), dormant = off - base (switch unset), total = par - base.
